title: Formula Corpus Entry
description: The schema for a single formula in the corpus. It is written as YAML and validated against this schema after parsing.

id.description: The FROZEN numeric identity. This is the value that enters the wire format. Once assigned it NEVER changes, and it is NEVER reused even after retirement. The block convention: 0x0100-01FF elliptic curves, 0x0200-02FF modular arithmetic and RSA, 0x0300-03FF hash and MAC, 0x0400-04FF lattice and post-quantum, 0x0500-05FF classical ciphers, 0x0600-06FF symmetric and stream ciphers, 0x0700-07FF transport (raw data, not a formula), 0x0800-08FF protocols and proofs. 0xFFFF is RESERVED for the wire format's chain mode and no corpus entry may take it.

slug.description: A human readable identity. It is used in the filename and in logs and NEVER enters the wire format.

version.description: The entry version. If params or constraints change, a NEW ID is opened rather than the entry being edited; this field only rises for corrections inside the doc block.

status.description: active: in use. deprecated: not used for new encryption, kept for decoding. retired: a historical record only, the id stays blocked.

doc.description: LAYER 3, for the RAG and for humans. The engine never reads this block.

domain.description: The top level category; it has to match the id block.

summary.description: 1 to 3 sentences. The field the RAG search feeds on most.

notes.description: A longer explanation, the traps, the history. Optional.

references.description: Book, paper and RFC citations, so the RAG can cite a source.

related.description: The numeric ids of related formulas.

params.description: LAYER 1, the engine. LIST ORDER IS WIRE ORDER and it is significant. A parameter referred to by another has to come BEFORE it (the backward reference rule). All widths are FIXED, because variable length leaks the magnitude of the parameter.

name.description: It has to match the symbol in the latex field.

type.description: prime: a prime modulus. field_element: an element of F_p, requires 'mod'. scalar: an integer modulo the group order, requires 'mod'. uint: a fixed width unsigned integer. point: a curve point, requires 'curve', in compressed SEC1 encoding. enum: one of 'values'. bytes: a fixed length octet string.

bits.description: The FIXED width on the wire. Required for prime, field_element, scalar, uint and bytes. For point it is derived as bits+8, and for enum from the length of values.

mod.description: For field_element and scalar: the name of the earlier parameter carrying the modulus.

curve.description: For point: a name pointing at the group of earlier parameters defining the curve.

values.description: The allowed values for enum. The index is what travels on the wire.

role.description: public: written into the ciphertext. secret: not written, derived from the key. derived: not written, computed from the other parameters. Only 'public' ones enter the payload.

constraints.description: LAYER 1, the validity rules. They run through a restricted AST evaluator and raw eval() is NEVER used. They are checked before encryption and after decoding.

expr.description: A Python expression. Only names from params and arithmetic or comparison operators may be used.

reason.description: The explanation shown to the user when it is violated.

sampler.description: LAYER 2, the distinguisher. How valid parameter sets are sampled to build a training corpus.

strategy.description: uniform_valid: rejection sampling until the constraints hold. from_catalog: only the known values in 'catalog'. mixed: a combination of the two.

catalog.description: Named ready made parameter sets for from_catalog and mixed (secp256k1, P-256 and so on).

max_rejections.description: The give up threshold for uniform_valid. Exceeding it means the entry's constraints are too narrow.
